name: Azure Courtyard Estate
generationBrief:
Design and construct an extraordinary contemporary Caribbean waterfront estate in Saint Lucia with an estimated property value of US$25 million.

The property occupies a spacious waterfront site with ocean views and a gently sloping landscape.

Create a sophisticated luxury residence with approximately six generous bedroom suites, expansive living and entertainment spaces, a memorable entrance, exceptional indoor-outdoor connections, substantial terraces, a spectacular infinity pool and integrated tropical landscaping.

Develop a coherent architectural concept with impressive massing, coordinated building volumes, beautiful proportions, interesting elevations, sophisticated materials and an unmistakable luxury-estate presence.

You have creative freedom over the building composition, number of levels, architectural style, roof forms and overall arrangement.

Construct the complete, editable 3D exterior architecture rather than a small conceptual representation.

architecturalPlan.scaleRationale: The US$25m figure is treated as a marker of exceptional architectural ambition, not a construction budget or area formula. The estate is sized as a 776 m² single-level composition: a 392 m² central entertaining pavilion and two 192 m² suite pavilions, providing capacity for six generous suites while retaining broad outdoor rooms. The supplied waterfront setting supports a low, view-oriented campus rather than a tall object. Site dimensions, exact shoreline, survey, setbacks, wind and flood levels are unprovided assumptions.
architecturalPlan.arrivalAndCirculation: All occupied slabs have a 0.20 m walking datum above the temporary flat ground plane. A landward driveway arrives directly at the central pavilion's protected front entrance, main-living-glass-2. The suite pavilions have separate covered front entrances, suite-west-glass-1 and suite-east-glass-1, reached by the shared arrival court and dry exterior circulation. The pool terrace is entered through the real rear garden opening main-rear-garden-panel. No upper occupied level is proposed, avoiding unresolved stair access.
architecturalPlan.volumeHierarchy: A 28 x 14 m, 4.20 m-high central living pavilion is the dominant datum. Two lower 12 x 16 m, 3.40 m-high private pavilions sit with 3 m clear lateral separation from the main pavilion's roof edges. The living roof ridge rises 1.20 m above its eaves; the suite roofs rise 1.00 m. A 14 x 2.4 m supported pool-terrace canopy marks the transition from enclosed living to the water.
architecturalPlan.relationshipsAndViews: The arrival sequence is organized on the +Z side of the central pavilion; the ocean-facing outdoor sequence extends through the rear garden door, shaded terrace, pool near deck and rectangular basin toward -Z. The two suite pavilions frame this shared outdoor room without crossing the pool footprint. The pool's far edge is composed as the view edge, but no shoreline, actual ocean water, horizon, hydraulic overflow, or surveyed slope is represented.
architecturalPlan.roofFacadeAndMaterials: The composition uses pale limestone envelopes, warm timber roof and canopy planes, and bronze-toned frames/screens implied by the selected palette. Broad hip and gable roofs with deep 0.9–1.4 m eaves provide a Caribbean climate response. Front facade bays establish a formal arrival rhythm; the pool facade is replaced with a deep, real garden-door opening and flanking limestone piers. Suite rears receive wide but fixed glazed view bays, while their actual entries remain on the arrival side.

physicalProgramme.basis: Six suite capacity is reserved across two 192 m² private pavilion slabs, three suites per pavilion. The 392 m² central slab accommodates the shared living, dining, entertaining and service capacity. Allocations are capacity commitments for exterior-designed envelopes, not completed interior room measurement or fit-out. The stated property value is not used as an area or cost calculation.

programme.name: Central living and entertainment pavilion
programme.strategy: Dominant enclosed pavilion with formal arrival facade and pool-facing garden passage.
programme.limitation: Interior living, dining, bar, kitchen and entertainment fit-out is intentionally deferred.

programme.name: Bedroom suite capacity — west pavilion
programme.strategy: Three-suite capacity reserved in the west private pavilion with formal arrival door and broad fixed view glazing.
programme.limitation: Three distinct suites, bathrooms, dressing rooms and internal corridors are not partitioned in exterior scope.

programme.name: Bedroom suite capacity — east pavilion
programme.strategy: Three-suite capacity reserved in the east private pavilion with formal arrival door and broad fixed view glazing.
programme.limitation: Three distinct suites, bathrooms, dressing rooms and internal corridors are not partitioned in exterior scope.

programme.name: Arrival court and driveway
programme.strategy: A broad limestone drive aligns to the central protected entry and keeps arrival separate from the pool terrace.
programme.limitation: Vehicle turning geometry, gates, lighting and planting are not modeled.

programme.name: Shaded outdoor living terrace
programme.strategy: A datum-matched terrace joins the rear garden opening to the pool near deck beneath a supported canopy.
programme.limitation: Outdoor furniture, kitchen/bar fit-out and movable shade are deferred.

programme.name: Rectangular infinity-effect pool
programme.strategy: A constructed rectangular basin, coping and dry perimeter terminate the terrace sequence at the view-facing far edge.
programme.limitation: The far edge is a visual infinity-effect composition only; overflow troughs, pumps, filtration, hydraulics, safety certification and ocean connection are not represented.

programme.name: Tropical landscape reserve
programme.strategy: Shallow perimeter planting beds reserve soft landscape zones around arrival and pool spaces.
programme.limitation: Plant species, trees, irrigation, soil, terrain grading and mature tropical planting are not supported as constructed scene elements.

designDecisions.decision: Used the value only to justify a bespoke estate-scale composition with a dominant living pavilion, suite pavilions and resolved outdoor sequence.
designDecisions.limitation: No valuation, cost estimate or luxury certification is claimed.

designDecisions.decision: Placed arrival and private suite entries on one side of the composition and directed terrace and pool sequence toward the assumed water view.
designDecisions.limitation: No surveyed shore, flood datum, setback or marine work is modeled.

designDecisions.decision: Constructed a rectangular basin with floor, perimeter walls, coping and dry decks at the end of the terrace sequence.
designDecisions.limitation: Overflow hydraulics and a true engineered infinity edge are unsupported.

designDecisions.decision: Used deep roof eaves, shaded terrace canopy and selective view glazing for a climate-responsive exterior.
designDecisions.limitation: Wind, corrosion, thermal and hurricane performance are not verified.

designDecisions.decision: Organized a legible sequence of drive, arrival, shared living, shade and pool, with private pavilions subordinate to the central volume.
Replaced the central rear wall with a fitted, real garden-door bay facing the terrace and pool.
designDecisions.limitation: The adjacent glazing is limited to the constructed bay; no glare or view simulation is provided.

designDecisions.decision: Considered a mono-pitch ventilated roof; selected coordinated hip and gable roofs instead to distinguish the central pavilion from quieter suite pavilions.
designDecisions.limitation: Ventilated ridge, gutters and rainwater systems are not constructed.

designDecisions.decision: Applied the principle of a clear vehicle approach terminating at a protected pedestrian threshold.
designDecisions.limitation: No gate, turning analysis, lighting or planted median is constructed.
